rows.title_full: AN ACT REDEFINING THE TERM 'VETERAN' THEREBY AMENDING FURTHER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6948 AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to clarify the definition of VETERAN in order to reconcile inconsistencies in the definition as stated in RAs 6948, 7696 vis-a-vis Section 7 of the Constitution. It defines VETERAN as ANY PERSON WHO IS A WAR VETERAN OR A VETERAN OF A MILITARY CAMPAIGN OR WHO RENDERED MILITARY SERVICE IN THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES. A WAR VETERAN IS ANY PERSON WHO RENDERED MILITARY SERVICE IN THE LAND, SEA OR AIR FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINE WHEN THE PHILIPPINES WAS AT WAR AND FOREIGN NATIONALS WHOO SERVED IN THE PHILIPPINE FORCES. A VETERAN OF A MILITARY CAMPAIGN IS ANY PERSON WHO BECAME PART OF THE PHILIPPINE EXPEDITIONARY FORCES SENT ABROAD OR WHO RENDERED SERVICE IN A PHILIPPINE MILITARY UNIT WHEN SAID UNIT PARTICIPATED IN A MILITARY CAMPAIGN SO DESIGNATED BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE PHILIPPINES. A VETERAN WHO RENDERED MILITARY SERVICE IN THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES IS ONE WHO HAS BEEN HONORABLY DISCHARGED OR SEPARATED AFTER HAVING AVAILED THE MANDATORY OR OPTIONAL RETIREMENT PROGRAM.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04451

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 209 AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 227, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, THEREBY LIMITING MARRIAGE TO NATURAL BORN MALES AND NATURAL BORN FEMALES
rows.abstract: This bill prohibits marriages abetween two men, one of whom had a sex exchange operation and between two women, one of whom also had a sex exchange operation.  With recent developments in the field of medicine, it is now possible to alter or  change a person's sexual organ to make it appear as that of the opposite sex. With this, we have directly challeged the laws of God, of nature and even of man.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-08-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT PREVENTING AND PENALIZING COMPUTER FRAUD, ABUSES AND OTHER CYBER-RELATED FRAUDULENT ACTIVITIES, AND CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE CYBER-CRIME INVESTIGATION AND COORDINATING CENTER, PRESCRIBING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Cyber Crime Act of 2001.\" This bill seeks to protect and safeguard the integrity of computers, computer systems, computer networks, computer servers, database, and information and data stores from computer users who resort to computer fraud, abuses and other cyber-related fraudulent activities, by providing penal sanctions to the perpetrators. It creates a coordinating body, the Cyber-Crime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC), which shall coordinate, collate and synergize efforts of all law enforcement agencies in combating cyber crimes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on INFORMATION COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY since 2005-01-12

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING ALL DISPOSABLE LANDS OF THE GOVERNMENT WHICH HAVE REMAINED IDLE AND SUITABLE FOR RESIDENTIAL PURPOSES SHALL BE DEVELOPED INTO SOCIALIZED HOUSING SITE FOR LOW-SALARIED GOVERNMENT AND PRIVATE EMPLOYEES AND SQUATTERS
rows.title_short: The Idle Disposable Public Land Conversion Act
rows.abstract: \"The Idle Disposable Public Land Conversion Act.\" Declares it a policy of the State to promote the housing needs of its inhabitants specifically the low-salaried employees in both the public and the private sectors including squatters in the urban areas. Directs the National Housing Authority, after pinpointing the idle disposable public lands, to publish the areas for socialized housing projects and thereafter allocate such lands to qualified applicants for their housing needs.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on 2005-05-17

committee_action.remarks: for consolidation with HB No. 1596 and for reporting out

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 70 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991 AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to improve the recall mechanism as mandated in the 1991 Local Government Code. Increases the percentage number of required voters to validate a recall proportionate to the number of the population of the local government unit whose elected official is the subject of a recall process.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C015
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09346) enacted on 2006-06-24
rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE DEATH PENALTY REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7659 ENTITLED, 'AN ACT TO IMPOSE THE DEATH PENALTY ON CERTAIN HEINOUS CRIMES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED, OTHER SPECIAL PENAL LAWS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill abolishes death penalty and, in lieu thereof, imposes the penalty of reclusion perpetua. Justice must likewise be tempered with mercy in order for genuine repentance and change to have a chance to prosper. Hence, emphasis must be placed on restorative justice rather than retributive justice.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04826

rows.author: C015
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2005-12-14, transmitted to on 2006-01-19 and received by the Senate on 2006-01-19
rows.title_full: OMNIBUS HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT ACT
rows.title_short: Omnibus Housing and Urban Development Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Omnibus Housing and Urban Development Act of 2004.\" Declares it a policy of the State to: 1)undertake a comprehensive and continuing program of housing and urban development which will make available at affordable cost, decent housing and basic services; 2) adopt workable policies that will guarantee the rationalization and optimum utilization of land and resources; 3) develop a sustainable and viable housing finance system that shall tap alternative, including non-traditional, sources of funds, for the government's housing program; 4) rationalize and strengthen the urban development and shelter delivery system  by enhancing local autonomy and decentralization and providing local government units more power, authority, responsibility and resources; and 5) institutionalize the citizenry's involvement at all levels of the urban planning and development process.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04264

rows.abstract: \"Education Trust Fund Act.\" This bill defines the fund as the accumulated money deducted from GSIS and the SSS members and paid to the system for the education of the grantees, then paid to colleges or universities for a vocational, technical or baccalaureate program as provided in the policy contract.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING MERCHANDISING STORES FROM CHARGING MORE THAN THE RETAIL PRICE OF GOODS PURCHASED WITH CREDIT CARDS AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR ANY VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: This bill declares it unlawful for any merchandising store to charge customers with more than the actual retail price of the goods purchased when such purchase is done with the use of a credit card. Imposes a punishment of 6 months to 1 year imprisonment or a fine of P20,000 to P100,000.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D071
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING PREFERENCE OF EMPLOYMENT TO ANY ONE CHILD OF VETERANS IN THE GOVERNMENT, INCLUDING GOVERNMENT-OWNED AND/OR CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Extending Preference of Employment to Any One Child of Veterans in the Government
rows.abstract: This bill declares it a policy of the State to enhance the socio-economic security and well-being of veterans and their families, thus all government agencies, including government-owned and/or controlled corporations are directed to hire or employ any child of a veteran.  In the absence or disqualification of said child, a grandchild shall be hired or employed in his stead.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-30, transmitted to on 2006-09-07 and received by the Senate on 2006-09-07

rows.author: D046
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7898 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'AFP MODERNIZATION ACT'
rows.abstract: This bill amends R.A. 7898 to attain the following, among others: 1) fix the annual appropriation for the AFP Modernization Act in an amount not less than 0.3% of the last officially reported gross national product; 2) establish a research and development program to upgrade existing AFP inventory of equipment and weapon systems; 3) expand the sources of funding for the AFP Modernization Act Trust Fund to include the proceeds from the lease and/or joint venture agreements and such other dispositions pertaining to military camps; 4) adopt a Defense Acquisition System which shall be separate and distinct from the procurement system applicable to other departments of government; and 5) create the office of the Undersecretary in the Department of National Defense for Resource Management and Capability Development.

rows.abstract: \"Military Real Estate Development Act.\" To raise funds for the AFP Modernization Program, the bill authorizes the President of the Philippines to identify military real estate or parts thereof that could be disposed of and/or commercially developed based on established criteria for disposal.

rows.abstract: This bill directs the mandatory appointment of a social welfare development officer in every provincial, city AND MUNICIPAL GOVERNMENT.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 263 OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 442, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES THEREOF
rows.abstract: This bill provides that a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) may stipulate that no labor union may strike and no employer may declare a lockout: Provided, that 1) the said agreement is negotiated in the collective bargaining agreement; 2) the \"no strike-no lockout\" agreement is limited to matters which are economic in nature or one which is conducted to force wage or other concessions from the employer not granted by the law itself; 3) the \"no strike-no lockout\" agreement shall exist only for a period of time; and 4) the \"no strike clause\" shall be operative only in times of national unemployment emergency.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 13 (a), TITLE V, BOOK III OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: This bill protects the rights of Filipino Interior Designers by setting forth conditions under which foreigners may perform professional services as interior designers or consultants in the country. Requires foreigners to secure a special temporary permit from the Professional Regulation Commission to practice their profession
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2005-05-04

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AN EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS PLAN TO PREVENT AND SUPPRESS THE SPREAD OF EMERGENCY INFECTIOUS DISEASES AND OTHER EPIDEMICS
rows.title_short: Infectious Disease Emergency Preparedness Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Infectious Disease Emergency Preparedness Act of 2004.\" This bill authorizes the isolation and quarantine of those infected as measures to control infectious diseases.  It establishes an emergency preparedness plan to prevent and suppress the spread of infectious diseases and other epidemics by undertaking medical examination and treatment of overseas Filipino workers while abroad, and authorizes the arrest, apprehension, detention or conditional release of individuals to prevent the introduction, transmission or spread of suspected infectious diseases.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C137
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR FIREARMS REGULATION AND EXEMPTING SELECTED PERSONS AND ENTITIES FROM THE GENERAL PROHIBITION AGAINST CARRYING OF FIREARMS
rows.abstract: This bill identifies the persons who are exempted from the general prohibition to carry firearms in public. It also provides the standards for the issuance of a firearms license and permit to carry firearms.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2004-08-02

rows.abstract: Rationale:  Retired government officials, employees and workers deserve the concern of the government for their welfare and well-being, as they had devoted and dedicated the best years of their lives working under the government in the service of the people.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-08-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING THE TERM OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND SETTING OF THE DATE OF THE ELECTION OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9164
rows.abstract: This bill extends the term of all barangay officials from three (3) years to five (5) years so that election for these offices shall be held every five (5) years.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03742

rows.author: D089
rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING CERTAIN ACTS OR TRANSACTIONS IN GOVERNMENT OFFICES AS 'FIXING' AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Fixing Law of 2004.\" This bill defines fixing as any arrangement and/or agreement whereby relative immunity from application of the law is obtained or that which hastens and facilitates processes in government transactions through the use of corrupt methods or employment of economic and social influence to public officials and employees, law enforcement officers and other authorities for the benefit of another person who is in legal difficulty or who seeks political or economic favor or concession.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D089
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE PUBLICATION, SALE OR DISTRIBUTION, PRODUCTION, IMPORTATION AND EXHIBITION OF OBSCENE AND PORNOGRAPHIC MATERIALS AND THE DEMONSTRATION, PERFORMANCE OR EXHIBITION IN PUBLIC INDECENT AND SEXUAL ACTS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Obscenity and Pornography Act of 2004.\" This bill declares it a State policy to safeguard the morality of society, particularly the youth and women, against the eroding influence of immoral doctrines, obscene and pornographic publications and indecent shows. It seeks to prohibit the public demonstration of sexual acts, the distribution, sale and production of pornographic materials and provides penalties for violations.
rows.status: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-05-20

committee_action.action: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-05-20

rows.author: D089
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE CREATION OF THE NATIONAL INDEPENDENT COMMISSION AGAINST CORRUPTION, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: National Independent Commission Against Corruption Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"National Independent Commission Against Corruption Act of 2004.\" This bill creates a Commission which is mandated to implement and coordinate, at the national level, the prevention, control and elimination of graft and corrupt practices at all levels in government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT REORGANIZATION since 2004-08-02

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NUMBERED SIXTEEN HUNDRED TWO, PRESCRIBING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR JUETENG, AND OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Jueteng Act of 2004.\" Declares it the policy of the State to eradicate jueteng, promote local revenues through honest, legitimate, lawful and ethical means and impose heavier sanctions and penalties on local administrators and law enforcers who provide protection to jueteng operators and syndicates.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-08-02

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: AN ACT LIBERALIZING AND ACCELERATING THE PROCESSING AND DEPLOYMENT OF OVERSEAS FILIPINO CONTRACT WORKERS, AND APPROPRIATING THE NECESSARY FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"OFW Liberation Act of 2004.\" This bill amends the Migrant Workers Act by clarifying the State's policy as regards overseas employment. By virtue of this Act, the State shall actively promote overseas employment to achieve national development. Directs the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) to pursue programs and policies that simplify the requirements for overseas employment.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on 2006-09-20

rows.abstract: \"Coast Guard Modernization Act.\" This bill aims to give the Philippine Coast Guard a fighting chance at being the best it can be by providing for the modernization of its equipment and training, and the allocation of the necessary funds for this purpose.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2005-01-12

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING PHILIPPINE EMBASSIES ANS CONSULATES TO CONDUCT CLASSES FOR CHILDREN OF FILIPINOS IN OTHER COUNTRIES, TO EDUCATE THEM ON PHILIPPINE HISTORY, CULTURE, LANGUAGES AND CIVICS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill requires all Philippine embassies and consulates, particularly in countries where there are Filipino expatriates, to conduct special classes, free of charge, during Saturdays for children of Filipino parentage to educate them on Philippine history, languages, culture and civics.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on 2006-04-20

committee_action.remarks: Transmitted to the Committee on Appropriations on 2006-03-06

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE NATIONAL PROGRAM FOR FILIPINO GIFTED CHILDREN AND SCIENCE-ORIENTED YOUTH, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Gifted Children and Science-Oriented Youth Act
rows.abstract: \"Gifted Children and Science-Oriented Youth Act.\" This bill enumerates the following objectives: a) identify the gifted Filipino children and science-oriented youth; b) establish a Center for the identification and nurturance of these children; c) provide scholarship grants and other forms of assistance for gifted children; d) provide funds for research and development, curriculum development, training of parents, teachers and other personnel and the necessary infrastructure; e) provide incentives to government institutions and the private sector that participate in the implementation of this Act, and f) establish and maintain linkages with national and international institutions involved in progress on giftedness.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on EDUCATION AND WELFARE OF SPECIAL PERSONS since 2004-11-09

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING COMMERCIAL HANDLINE FISHING AND VESSEL AND PROVIDING REGULATIONS FOR UTILIZATION THEREOF, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE 'THE PHILIPPINE FISHERIES CODE OF 1998'
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to give weight to traditional fishing practices and small fishermen by defining handline commercial fishing as a traditional passive fishing method which utilizes a single fishing line and attached hook; and handline commercial vessel as a commercial fishing vessel which exclusively utilizes the commercial handline fishing method.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04067

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING ADDITIONAL SAFEGUARDS TO THE INTER-COUNTRY ADOPTION OF FILIPINO CHILDREN, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE INTER-COUNTRY ADOPTION ACT OF 1995
rows.abstract: This bill prohibits MEMBERS OF THE BOARD, INCLUDING THE AGENCIES, INSTITUTIONS AND ORGANIZATIONS TO WHICH ANY MEMBER IS PRESENTLY OR WAS PREVIOUSLY ASSOCIATED, FROM RECEIVING MONEY, DONATION OR OTHER BENEFITS, DIRECT OR INDIRECTLY, BY REASON OF HIS OFFICE OF THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE INTER-COUNTRY ADOPTION LAW.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A SEPARATE NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL IN BARANGAY TINAGACAN, GENERAL SANTOS CITY, TO BE KNOWN AS THE TINAGACAN NATIONAL HIGH SCHOOL AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.status: Substituted by HB05042

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 4 AND 6, PARAGRAPH (c) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6972, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'BARANGAY-LEVEL TOTAL DEVELOPMENT AND PROTECTION OF CHILDREN ACT', AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill increases the allowance of day care workers to PHP2,000.00 and mandates the Sangguniang Bayan or Sangguniang Panglungsod to create one mandatory position of Barangay Day Care Worker in every barangay.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT REAPPORTIONING THE LEGISLATIVE DISTRICTS THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY AMONG PROVINCES AND CITIES
rows.abstract: This bill envisions to achieve equality of representation, a basic principle of republicanism, through the reapportionment of districts which, following the constitutional requirement, shall, as far as practicable, be comprised of contiguous, compact and adjacent territories.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2005-03-02

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FREE TUITION AND OTHER FEES TO CHILDREN OF TEACHERS AND EMPLOYEES IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE INSTITUTIONS OF HIGHER LEARNING
rows.abstract: This bill extends educational assistance to children of our mentors in the form of tuition fee exemption and discounts to enable them to obtain a college education with less financial and psychological strain on their parents. It also extends the same privileges to children of other employees of educational institutions, who, in their own capacity, facilitate the educational attainment of our children.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE SHOWING OF TELEVISION ADVERTISEMENTS FEATURING SEX AND/OR VIOLENCE TO CHILDREN OF TENDER AGE
rows.abstract: \"Television Advertisement Regulation Act of 2004.\" This bill regulates the showing of film or movie advertisements or trailers on television depicting sex and violence by restricting their viewing to hours when children of formative years are not usually watching television. Directs the Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) to implement the provisions of this Act and imposes a stiffer penalty for violation thereof.
rows.status: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-05-20

committee_action.action: Under study by the Technical Working Group(TWG) on 2005-05-20

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MANDATORY AUTOPSY OF ANY PERSON WHO DIED IN A VIOLENT, SUSPICIOUS, QUESTIONABLE, UNUSUAL AND/OR UNNATURAL MANNER, THE CONDITIONS FOR THE PROPER ISSUANCE OF THE DEATH CERTIFICATE OF SAID PERSON AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Autopsy Act of 2004.\" Rationale: The autopsy shall be conducted in a manner that will ensure the proper determination of the cause, manner and other surrounding circumstances of death, and must rule out every other possible and conceivable contributing cause.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7610 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS 'THE SPECIAL PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AGAINST CHILD ABUSE, EXPLOITATION AND DISCRIMINATION ACT', AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: This bill enumerates additional remedial measures to correct the deplorable manner by which local government and law enforcement officials, as well as members of the justice sector, handle cases of child rape and sexual molestations and child prostitution involving minors below the age of twelve (12).  It provides for the issuance of an automatic hold order for those accused to prevent them from fleeing abroad.  Furthermore, it imposes the maximum penalty on law enforcers and members of the Judiciary Department found guilty including willfully abetting these crimes or causing or assisting in the plight of those accused.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2004-08-02

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING PRE-AUDIT ON ALL GOVERNMENT PROGRAMS AND PROJECTS WITH FUNDING REQUIREMENTS BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES  FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.abstract: This bill declares that any official or employee who approves or allows the implementation of a certain program or project with government funding without undergoing pre-audit shall for the first offense, suffer the penalty of suspension from office for a period of not less than fifteen (15) days nor more than sixty (60) days; for second of succeeding offenses, the penalty of imprisonment of not less than six (6) months but not more than six (6) years shall be imposed on the offender, plus perpetual disqualification to hold public office.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-08-00

rows.author: D003
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A MORE RESPONSIVE AND COMPREHENSIVE REGULATION FOR THE PRACTICE OF CHEMICAL ENGINEERING IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: \"Revised Chemical Engineering Law.\" Rationale: The present advances in technology practically make all phases of engineering work fully automated. The availability of advanced, sophisticated and modern instruments has rendered Republic Act No. 318 obsolete, sometimes irrelevant and impractical. A review of the law would reveal that some provisions thereof are inapplicable and therefore prone to be violated than followed.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-08-02
